title: Take one photo with a single-use film camera: hold it, wind its thumbwheel to the stop, press the shutter
instruction: Wind this single-use film camera on to the next frame and fire its shutter once, then leave it standing on the table.
context: Snapping a photo with a disposable camera at a wedding, a party or on holiday is familiar to most people. The FunSaver's instructions, printed on its back, boil down to advancing the film and pressing the shutter: "advance it with the thumbwheel until it stops turning. Then look through the viewfinder and click a picture"; "The film advance wheel is interlocked with the shutter mechanism" (review), so the shutter stays locked until the wheel is at its stop. The hand skill: the ridged 24 mm thumbwheel stands only 3 mm proud of the back and turns only when a fingertip pressed on its edge is drawn sideways, so a frame takes many short strokes (about 1.5 turns, our estimate), each lifted and repeated without slipping off. Every stroke pushes the 117 g camera, which slides away on the table, so one hand holds it while the other strokes, then presses the shutter and lets the camera stand.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Kodak FunSaver single-use camera (27 exposures, yellow/black plastic, 117 g), loose, standing on its base, lens toward +x, back toward the robot: body 12 cm along y, 5.9 cm tall, 3.0 cm deep plus a 0.5 cm lens barrel; centre at x 22.5, y 2.0; back at x 21.0. Thumbwheel: black, ridged, 2.4 cm across, 0.7 cm thick, vertical axis at x 21.9, y -2.4, in a recess at the top-back-right corner, 0.3 cm proud of the back, top 0.15 cm under the camera's top. Shutter button: 0.9 x 0.9 cm, 0.15 cm proud of the top, centre x 22.9, y 1.2. The last frame was fired: wheel unwound, shutter locked. Flash off. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step: the camera's pose, the thumbwheel's and the shutter button's joint angles, each finger's collision-hull points. Best of: 0.4 the wheel wound to its stop (within 2 deg of 540 deg, one frame); 0.6 the shutter fired after winding (button 1.0 mm down while wound: a photo); 1.0 (success, held 1 s) exactly one photo, the camera standing on its base on the table (tilt under 10 deg, lowest point within 3 mm of the table), every finger point 1 cm or more from it, still (under 1 mm in 1 s). Pressing before winding does nothing (0); a second photo keeps 0.6; doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a photo is the shutter's click on the trial video's sound (and the counter one lower); with no click, the operator presses the shutter after the trial with the lens covered: a click then means wound but not fired (0.4), none means not wound (0). Standing, let go and still from the video.
reset_notes: If the wheel was left partly wound, wind it to the stop; press the shutter with the lens covered (this is also the post-trial check) so the camera starts unwound with its shutter locked; flash off; stand it on its taped outline, lens away from the robot. Each trial uses one of the camera's 27 frames; replace the camera when the counter reaches 0. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The camera is boxes and cylinders at the FunSaver's size and mass; the wheel has 36 ridges. Estimates: 540 deg (1.5 turns) per frame, 0.01 N m wheel friction, the anti-reverse pawl and the stop as a stiff spring (2 N m/rad), the shutter's spring (2.5 N to start, 3.5 N at 1.0 mm, firing at 1.0 mm) and its lock (a spring needing about 100 N for 1 mm). No film, no click, no flash; the frame counter is tracked, not shown.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left gripper took hold of the camera and moved it about, tilting it, and the right gripper came near it; the thumbwheel never reached its stop and the shutter never fired); demo: 1.0
